Support

Most support problems have one obvious home, and it is usually not us. Trycord is self-hostable, so the instance you are on is run by someone. Start there, and escalate only if they cannot help.

Start here: which kind of instance are you on?

This decides who can actually fix your problem.

  • An official instance — run by the project or a partner, and listed in the app. One organisation operates all of them, so you can escalate straight to us. See the official instance terms.
  • Your own, or a community’s — run by whoever set it up. They are the operator, they control the data, and they are the only ones who can change anything.

Not sure? The instance’s name and owner are shown in the app, and self-hosted instances usually name their own admin contact.

Account, community, or content problem

A ban, a timeout, a deleted message, a role you think you should have, a channel you cannot see. This is moderation, and it is the instance operator or the community moderators — not the project. They can undo what they did; we cannot.

Report it in the app where you can, or contact the operator directly. OPERATOR: your contact address

Appealing a moderation decision

If an account, community, or message was actioned, you can appeal. Start at the appeal form.

  • You need the action ID from the enforcement notice.
  • You do not need to be signed in to submit an appeal — being banned should not stop you appealing.
  • Signed-in users can review past decisions under My appeals.
  • On an official instance, appeals are reviewed centrally, so a community you were removed from cannot refuse to hear you.
  • Appeals are reviewed by a person. Expect a real answer, not an autoresponder.

Something is broken

Work down this list; it finds the cause most of the time.

  1. Check the status page. If the instance is degraded, nothing you do locally will help.
  2. Reload, and try a private window. A stale cached build or a stuck service worker causes a surprising share of “the app is broken” reports.
  3. If the desktop app misbehaves, update it. The desktop app does not auto-update mid-session, so an old build against a new server is a common cause of odd failures.
  4. Still stuck? Report it on GitHub. Include the instance URL, what you expected, what happened, and your app version — from Settings, Updates.

Privacy, your data, or a legal request

Access, export, correction, and deletion are handled by the operator of your instance, because they are the data controller. If you are self-hosting, that is you. See the Privacy Policy for what is held and for how long.

A request about an official instance can go to OPERATOR: the privacy contact for official instances. Formal legal notices go to OPERATOR: your address for formal legal notices.

Security report

Found a vulnerability? Read the security page first, then follow its reporting route. Please do not test against instances that have not agreed to it.

Still stuck?

Tell us what you tried and what happened. The most useful reports are short and specific: which instance, which action, what you expected, what you saw instead. “It doesn’t work” is much harder to act on than “scrolling the member list freezes the tab after about 200 rows”.

Operator note. This page is deliberately operator-agnostic, because it is served by every instance. Anyone running an instance can edit public/support.html to add their own address, email, or support hours where the placeholders appear.
